History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
50-year-old man with 5-day history of cough, coryza, sore throat, intermittent feverishness and mild shortness of breath; clinical impression is viral upper respiratory tract infection/early influenza; conservative care advised with standby amoxicillin if no improvement within 24–48 h.

History:
• Presenting complaints: “run-down,” cough, cold, sore throat, runny nose, intermittent hot/cold sweats, mild shortness of breath.  
• Onset/progression: Began Saturday evening (≈5 days ago); symptoms persist without significant improvement.  
• Cough: Mainly dry; “wee bit” sputum in mornings.  
• Upper airway: Runny nose; sore throat (voice strain from shouting at football); no self-inspection of pharynx.  
• Ears: Mild dullness/blocked sensation; no significant ear pain.  
• Respiratory: Mild shortness of breath; denies chest pain.  
• Constitutional: Feels feverish at night with blankets on/off; no temperature measured.  
• GI: One episode of diarrhea on day 1, now resolved; no nausea or vomiting; appetite intact, maintaining oral intake.  
• Musculoskeletal: Generalized stiffness in elbows/knees when bending; no focal joint pain.  
• Review of other systems: No abdominal pain, no focal neurological symptoms noted.

Past Medical History:
• Type 2 diabetes mellitus – on metformin.  
• Hypertension – previously documented “high blood pressure,” on lisinopril.  
• Overweight/obesity – self-reported “spare tyre”; no complications discussed.

Medications:
• Metformin – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Lisinopril – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Aspirin – “occasional,” dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
• No known drug allergies.

Social History:
• Lives with wife; adult children no longer at home.  
• Employment: Factory worker manufacturing steel parts.  
• Alcohol: ≈9 pints of beer per week (4 on Saturday, remainder Sunday).  
• Tobacco: Occasional cigarette use; currently transitioning to vaping to reduce smoking.  
• Recreational drugs: Not mentioned.

Family History:
• Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
(No objective examination performed/recorded during teleconsultation.)

Investigations:
• None ordered or reviewed.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Viral upper respiratory tract infection / probable early influenza
  • Advice: Rest, maintain hydration, regular paracetamol for fever/aches.  
  • Safety-net: If symptoms (particularly shortness of breath or fever) persist or worsen over next 24–48 h, start standby antibiotic.  
  • Prescription provided: Amoxicillin – 1 tablet three times daily for 5 days (dose/strength not documented) to start only if no improvement in 24–48 h.  
  • Follow-up: Return next week or sooner if deterioration (worsening SOB, persistent fever, chest pain, new productive cough with purulent sputum).

Issue 2: Type 2 diabetes mellitus
  • Continue metformin; ensure adequate hydration while unwell.  
  • Monitor blood sugars closely during illness (not explicitly discussed but implied good practice).

Issue 3: Hypertension
  • Continue lisinopril.  
  • Monitor blood pressure as usual.

General / Preventive
  • Smoking cessation encouraged; acknowledged progress with vaping.  
  • Limit alcohol intake per current guidelines.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing expected elements: vital signs, physical examination findings, objective temperature, medication doses/frequencies, blood glucose readings, vaccination status.  
• Internal conflicts: Patient first states breathing “fine,” later describes it as “not good” and short of breath – conflict noted. Cough described as “mostly dry” yet also admits to “wee bit” of sputum.  
• Transcript quality: Clear overall; conversational tangents and minor overlaps but clinically adequate.
